title: R Ashwin Demands BCCI Clarity on Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli's 2027 World Cup Futures
excerpt: R Ashwin demands clarity from BCCI on Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli's 2027 World Cup futures.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • R Ashwin demands clarity from BCCI on Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli's 2027 World Cup futures.
  • Selectors reportedly informed Rohit Sharma he may not be in ODI plans beyond the England series.
  • Ashwin defends both players' recent performances, calling Kohli 'excellent' and Rohit 'more than decent'.
  • He criticizes the BCCI for not communicating decisions about veterans sooner after the 2025 Champions Trophy.
The Uncertainty Surrounding India's ODI Veterans
›Rohit Sharma may play his last ODI on July 19, 2026.
›Selectors reportedly informed Rohit he is out of ODI plans.
›Ashwin calls for immediate clarity from BCCI on veteran players' futures.
›Kohli and Rohit have not been poor performers in ODIs.
https://x.com/yespunjab/status/2078127829401915715
  • Former India off-spinner R Ashwin has called on the BCCI to immediately clarify whether Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli are part of India's plans for the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa.
  • Ashwin said on his YouTube channel that if selectors had already decided to move on from the veterans, they should have communicated that right after the 2025 Champions Trophy victory — not left it until now.
  • The comments come amid reports that selectors have informed Rohit Sharma he is no longer in India's ODI plans beyond the current England series, with his Lord's match potentially being his last.
  • Ashwin insisted that both players' recent performances do not justify being sidelined, with Kohli "excellent" and Rohit "more than decent" in ODIs.

Ravichandran Ashwin has waded into the escalating debate over India's ODI future, urging the BCCI to stop letting speculation swirl around Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli and make a definitive call on whether both veterans will feature in the 2027 ODI World Cup squad.

Speaking on his YouTube channel "Ash Ki Baat" alongside journalist Vimal Kumar, the former India off-spinner questioned why India's cricket establishment had allowed uncertainty to build to this point when the tournament in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia is barely a year away.

"Why have we let it come till August 2026, when there are only 10-12 months to go for the 2027 World Cup in South Africa? Why have we let it come this far?"

— R Ashwin, on his YouTube channel "Ash Ki Baat"

The Communication Failure

Ashwin's comments arrive during one of the most turbulent weeks in recent Indian cricket. Reports surfaced earlier this week that the BCCI's senior selection committee had informed Rohit Sharma he was no longer part of their plans for the 2027 World Cup, with the third ODI against England at Lord's on July 19 potentially serving as his farewell appearance in Indian colors. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia has publicly dismissed the retirement speculation, but the conflicting signals have only deepened the confusion.

> **"Ashwin argued that one poor series should not define the trajectory of players who have carried India for over a decade.

"By pure performance, they have not been poor at all."**

The former off-spinner's central argument is one of basic professional courtesy. If selectors, the head coach, or the captain had already concluded that Rohit and Kohli would not be part of the World Cup squad, that conversation should have happened immediately after India's Champions Trophy 2025 victory — not leaked through media reports months later.

"If you ever felt, as a selector, coach, captain, or decision-maker, that I am not taking these players, if you feel that these players will not go to the 2027 World Cup and we don't want them, that could have been communicated at the end of the Champions Trophy," Ashwin said.

Defending the Veterans' Records

Ashwin pushed back firmly against any suggestion that recent form justified dropping either player. Both Rohit and Kohli have already retired from Test and T20I cricket, leaving ODIs as their sole remaining international format. Ashwin argued that one poor series should not define the trajectory of players who have carried India for over a decade.

"By pure performance, they have not been poor at all. Virat has been excellent. Rohit has been more than decent," he said.

He acknowledged that young opener Yashasvi Jaiswal is performing well and pushing hard for a place, alongside Ishan Kishan. But Ashwin framed that competition as a reason for more clarity, not less. Both the veterans and the younger players deserve transparent communication about where they stand, according to the former all-rounder.

Experience vs Youth at a World Cup

At the heart of Ashwin's argument is a conviction that major ICC tournaments demand seasoned performers who have handled pressure on the biggest stage. Kohli will be approaching 39 and Rohit past 40 by the time the tournament begins in October-November 2027, but Ashwin believes their experience outweighs age concerns.

"I personally think you need experienced batters to play the World Cup in South Africa," he said. "In all honesty, where does the speculation come from? Somewhere, it is in someone's mind that they should not go to the World Cup. I don't know who those people are."

He compared the situation to a marriage, saying that if the team management genuinely wants both players at the World Cup, they must make the decision now and ensure Rohit and Kohli feel "absolutely comfortable and confident" over the next year of preparation. Half-measures, he warned, would only create a cycle where every poor innings reignites doubt.

"If you do not make the decision now, it becomes difficult as the same thing will keep coming back after every one or two failures," Ashwin said.

What Happens Next

The immediate focus shifts to Lord's on July 19, where Rohit Sharma will bat in what media reports have framed as a potential farewell ODI. India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak has backed Rohit to deliver a strong performance, saying after the Cardiff ODI that fans should expect "a completely different innings" at Lord's.

Beyond that single match, the broader question Ashwin has raised remains unanswered. Chief selector Ajit Agarkar and head coach Gautam Gambhir have reportedly had conversations with both players about their Test retirements, but neither has publicly addressed the ODI selection question. For millions of Indian cricket fans worldwide, the uncertainty over two of the sport's biggest names heading into a World Cup year is becoming harder to watch than any result on the field.
